Rachel — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attaching our current order form draft (Orion_Draft_Order_Form_20250616.docx). Two quick areas our legal/product teams want to resolve before we bring this to procurement: 

1) Output ownership: the draft currently says "Customer owns Output" but Redwood has a paragraph that reserves the right to use de-identified outputs for product analytics. Can you confirm Redwood's intended scope (telemetry vs using customer outputs as training data)?

2) Training / feedback license: there's a present clause that grants "a perpetual, worldwide license to use Feedback for model improvement." We need clarification on whether that permits re-training models on raw customer prompts/outputs or only on aggregated signals. Also want an opt-in path if we want to allow a narrowly-scoped retrain later.

Samir flagged a separate ask — whether there's a telemetry-only exception where Redwood can keep short-lived caching for latency improvements but not persistent use for model training.

Can you propose language we can circulate? If easier, happy to take yours and pass to legal.

Thanks,
Alice

Hi Alice — appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (legal lead) + Jordan (deploy/ops) so we can give a single workback. High-level positions from our side: 

- Output: we accept "Customer owns Output" for customer-facing generated content. Redwood's usage should be limited to (a) short-term caching/KV for latency; (b) aggregated telemetry for service quality/bug fixes. We are sensitive to wholesale ingestion of raw outputs into model training unless explicitly opted-in.

- Training/Feedback license: our goal is to get non-exclusive rights to anonymized feedback/telemetry to improve the hosted service. We can offer an opt-in model retrain clause with clear scope and timebox (e.g., a one-off consent for a named rerun).

Next steps: Laura — can you propose redline language (short, contractual) that captures the above? Jordan — can you confirm what we can commit to for caching retention (time window) and telemetry export hygiene? Ben/Alice — would you like a short call tomorrow to close these items?

Team — attaching a redline I prepared (RI_redline_training_clause_v1.docx). Below are the suggested contractual snippets to send to Orion. I focused on concise, negotiable language. 

1) Output ownership (Order Form / Definitions):
"Customer Output" means content, text, images, and other artifacts generated by the Service in response to Customer inputs. Customer retains all rights, title and interest in Customer Output.

2) Redwood usage carveout — proposed clause (short):
"Redwood may retain ephemeral cached copies of Customer Input and Customer Output for up to forty-eight (48) hours solely to support low-latency request handling and debugging. Redwood may also collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry (including token-level latency metrics, system traces, and rate statistics) for service improvement, security, and product analytics. "

3) Feedback / Training license — proposed clause (negotiable):
"Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback for the limited purpose of improving and operating the Service, provided that such Feedback is aggregated or de-identified such that it does not constitute Customer Confidential Information. Redwood will not use raw Customer Input or Customer Output to train or improve models that are made generally available without Customer's prior written opt-in. Should Customer elect to opt in to a discrete model retrain, the parties will execute a separate written agreement specifying the scope, dataset, timebox, and compensation (if any)."

Rationale: keeps the standard model (customer owns output + Redwood can use telemetry) but blocks raw output/prompts from general model training without opt-in. Leaves room for a paid or scoped opt-in retrain.

Jordan: please confirm the 48-hour cache commitment is operationally achievable and whether we should tighten to 24 hours.

Ben/Rachel: if Orion is comfortable with these, we can send as our counterproposal.

--

Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the clear language; this gets us most of the way there. A couple of follow-ups from our product/legal review: 

- 48-hour cache: we appreciate the limit. For low-latency features we sometimes need a slightly longer rolling cache for session continuity (e.g., up to 7 days for ephemeral session stitching). Is Redwood able to commit to a hard cap of 7 days for session-level transient stores and confirm that this data will never be used in training without opt-in?

- Aggregated telemetry: can you explicitly call out that "aggregated, de-identified" excludes verbatim output snippets (i.e., not aggregated copies of outputs)? We want to avoid ambiguity where a high-frequency output could be included in an "aggregate" set and then used for training.

- Opt-in retrain: we like the separate written agreement approach. Could we add an audit right for any retrain that uses Customer-provided data? Simple line: "Customer may request an audit of the dataset used for a Customer-specific retrain to confirm de-identification and scope."

If you can incorporate these three bullets we can move to procurement. Happy to take the redline and mark it up on our side. 

On a process note: would Redwood prefer we do a single consolidated redline on the order form or send two short clauses like above for faster procurement review?

Thanks — Alice

Alice — appreciate the fast turnaround and precise asks. Quick summary of our commitments and next steps so procurement can move: 

1) Cache: we can do a hard cap of 7 days for session-level transient storage used strictly for session continuity/latency. We will not use session cache contents for model training absent Customer opt-in. Jordan confirms logging/retention controls and will update ops docs.

2) Aggregated telemetry: we'll clarify in the clause that "aggregated, de-identified telemetry" expressly excludes verbatim reproduction of Customer Output; examples (token-level latency histograms, counts, and vetted error traces) will be acceptable.

3) Opt-in retrain & audit right: we accept the audit request for any discrete retrain that includes Customer-provided data — audit scope limited to dataset composition and de-identification steps; audit timing and confidentiality process to be defined in the separate retrain agreement.

Next steps: Laura to incorporate Alice's bullet points into the redline. Ben and I will follow with a short <30 min call with Orion procurement Monday to close redlines and trigger DocuSign.
